title: 2 Corinthians Chapter 3 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on 2 Corinthians chapter 3 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: 2 Corinthians Chapter 3 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of 2 Corinthians Chapter 3.

questions.question: In 2 Corinthians 3, which of the following appears FIRST in the chapter?
options: Do we begin again to commend ourselves?
Ye are our epistle written in our hearts
Who also hath made us able ministers of the new testament
Not that we are sufficient of ourselves
questions.correctAnswer: Do we begin again to commend ourselves?
questions.explanation: This question refers to the first verse, 2 Corinthians 3:1, which begins with 'Do we begin again to commend ourselves?'.

questions.question: What are the believers described as in 2 Corinthians 3:2?
options: Able ministers of the new testament
questions.explanation: In 2 Corinthians 3:2, it states, 'Ye are our epistle written in our hearts,' indicating the believers are referred to as an epistle of Christ.

questions.question: According to 2 Corinthians 3:3, what is the epistle written with?
options: The Spirit of the living God
questions.correctAnswer: The Spirit of the living God
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 3:3 specifies that the epistle is 'written not with ink, but with the Spirit of the living God'.

questions.question: What kind of tables are mentioned in 2 Corinthians 3:3?
questions.explanation: The verse 2 Corinthians 3:3 mentions 'not in tables of stone, but in fleshy tables of the heart'.

questions.question: What do we have through Christ according to 2 Corinthians 3:4?
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 3:4 states, 'And such trust have we through Christ to God-ward:', highlighting the concept of trust.

questions.question: According to 2 Corinthians 3:5, where is our sufficiency from?
questions.explanation: The verse 2 Corinthians 3:5 indicates, 'but our sufficiency is of God', affirming that sufficiency comes from God.

questions.question: What has God made us according to 2 Corinthians 3:6?
options: Able ministers of the old testament
Able ministers of the new testament
questions.correctAnswer: Able ministers of the new testament
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 3:6 declares, 'Who also hath made us able ministers of the new testament', referring to our role as ministers.

questions.question: What does the letter do, according to 2 Corinthians 3:6?
questions.explanation: In 2 Corinthians 3:6, it is stated that 'for the letter killeth', making it clear that the letter has a negative effect.

questions.question: What does the spirit do, according to 2 Corinthians 3:6?
questions.explanation: The verse 2 Corinthians 3:6 contrasts the letter with the spirit, stating 'but the spirit giveth life'.

questions.question: Are letters of commendation needed according to 2 Corinthians 3:1?
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 3:1 poses the question about the need for letters of commendation, implying they are not necessary.

questions.question: Are we sufficient of ourselves according to 2 Corinthians 3:5?
questions.explanation: The text in 2 Corinthians 3:5 explicitly states, 'Not that we are sufficient of ourselves', indicating we are not sufficient by ourselves.

questions.question: Is it true that the believers are described as an epistle in 2 Corinthians 3:2?
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 3:2 states, 'Ye are our epistle written in our hearts', confirming that believers are indeed described as an epistle.

questions.question: Is it true that the spirit gives life according to 2 Corinthians 3:6?
questions.explanation: In 2 Corinthians 3:6, it is stated that 'the spirit giveth life', confirming that the spirit gives life.

questions.question: Is it false that the letter gives life according to 2 Corinthians 3:6?
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 3:6 clearly states that 'for the letter killeth', indicating that the letter does not give life.

questions.question: Is it false that we are sufficient of ourselves to think anything according to 2 Corinthians 3:5?
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 3:5 states 'Not that we are sufficient of ourselves', thus it is false to claim that we are sufficient of ourselves.

medium.title: 2 Corinthians Chapter 3 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from 2 Corinthians Chapter 3 to real-life situations.

questions.question: According to 2 Corinthians 3:7, what was the nature of the ministration of death written and engraven in stones?
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 3:7 states that the ministration of death was glorious, even though it was written and engraven in stones.

questions.question: What does 2 Corinthians 3:8 promise will happen if the ministration of death was glorious, as described in 2 Corinthians 3:7?
options: The ministration of the spirit will be rather glorious
The ministration of the spirit will be weak
The ministration of the spirit will be forgotten
The ministration of the spirit will be condemning
questions.correctAnswer: The ministration of the spirit will be rather glorious
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 3:8 follows 3:7 by promising that if the ministration of death was glorious, then the ministration of the spirit will be rather glorious.

questions.question: According to 2 Corinthians 3:9, how does the ministration of righteousness compare to the ministration of condemnation?
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 3:9 explains that if the ministration of condemnation is glory, much more does the ministration of righteousness exceed in glory.

questions.question: How does 2 Corinthians 3:10 explain the difference in glory between the old and the new ministration?
options: The old had no glory compared to the excelling glory of the new
questions.correctAnswer: The old had no glory compared to the excelling glory of the new
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 3:10 states that the old ministration, though made glorious, had no glory in comparison to the glory that excelleth in the new ministration.

questions.question: What practical hope does 2 Corinthians 3:12 say believers have because of the glory that remains?
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 3:12 says that seeing the hope they have, believers use great plainness of speech.

questions.question: According to 2 Corinthians 3:3, how are believers described in relation to the epistle of Christ?
options: Written not with ink but with the Spirit of the living God
questions.correctAnswer: Written not with ink but with the Spirit of the living God
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 3:3 describes believers as the epistle of Christ ministered by Paul and written not with ink but with the Spirit of the living God.

questions.question: What does 2 Corinthians 3:6 say about the letter and the spirit in the new testament ministry?
options: The letter killeth, but the spirit giveth life
The letter giveth life, but the spirit killeth
Both the letter and spirit killeth
Both the letter and spirit giveth life
questions.correctAnswer: The letter killeth, but the spirit giveth life
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 3:6 explains that the letter kills, but the spirit gives life, highlighting the difference between the old and new ministry.

questions.question: According to 2 Corinthians 3:5, in whom do ministers find their sufficiency?
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 3:5 states that ministers are not sufficient of themselves but their sufficiency is of God.

questions.question: How does 2 Corinthians 3:4 describe the confidence the ministers have?
options: They have trust through Christ to God-ward
They trust in their own abilities
They fear the judgment of men
They rely on letters of commendation
questions.correctAnswer: They have trust through Christ to God-ward
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 3:4 says the ministers have trust through Christ to God-ward.

questions.question: According to 2 Corinthians 3:11, what is said about the glory that remains compared to that which is done away?
options: That which remains is much more glorious
That which remains is less glorious
That which remains has no glory
questions.correctAnswer: That which remains is much more glorious
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 3:11 states that if the former glory was glorious, much more that which remains is glorious.

questions.question: What does 2 Corinthians 3:1 question about the need for letters of commendation?
options: Do we need letters of commendation to you or from you?
Should we write more letters of commendation?
Are letters of commendation only from others?
questions.correctAnswer: Do we need letters of commendation to you or from you?
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 3:1 asks if they begin to commend themselves again and if they need letters of commendation to or from the Corinthians.

questions.question: According to 2 Corinthians 3:2, how are the Corinthians described in relation to the ministers?
options: Ye are our epistle written in our hearts, known and read of all men
Ye are letters written on stone
questions.correctAnswer: Ye are our epistle written in our hearts, known and read of all men
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 3:2 says that the Corinthians are like an epistle written in the hearts of the ministers and known and read of all men.

questions.question: True or False: According to 2 Corinthians 3:12, because of the hope believers have, they speak with great plainness.
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 3:12 states that seeing the hope they have, believers use great plainness of speech.

questions.question: True or False: 2 Corinthians 3:6 teaches that the letter of the law gives life while the spirit kills.
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 3:6 says the letter killeth, but the spirit giveth life, opposite of the statement.

questions.question: True or False: 2 Corinthians 3:5 teaches that ministers are sufficient by themselves to think anything as of themselves.
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 3:5 states that ministers are not sufficient of themselves but their sufficiency is of God.

hard.title: 2 Corinthians Chapter 3 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from 2 Corinthians Chapter 3.

questions.question: What did Moses put over his face?
questions.explanation: Moses put a vail over his face to prevent the children of Israel from steadfastly looking at his countenance, as stated in 2 Corinthians 3:13.

questions.question: What remains unremoved in the reading of the Old Testament?
questions.explanation: The vail remains untaken away in the reading of the Old Testament, as mentioned in 2 Corinthians 3:14.

questions.question: What is done away in Christ?
questions.explanation: The vail is done away in Christ, as indicated in 2 Corinthians 3:14.

questions.question: Where the Spirit of the Lord is, what is present?
questions.explanation: Where the Spirit of the Lord is, there is liberty, as stated in 2 Corinthians 3:17.

questions.question: What happens to those who behold the glory of the Lord?
questions.explanation: Those who behold the glory of the Lord are changed into the same image from glory to glory, according to 2 Corinthians 3:18.

questions.question: What does the Greek word 'vail' (kalyptō) mean in 2 Corinthians 3:13?
questions.explanation: In 2 Corinthians 3:13, the Greek word 'kalyptō' means 'to cover', which refers to the vail Moses placed over his face.

questions.question: Which literary technique is used when comparing the glory of Moses with the glory of the Spirit?
questions.explanation: The comparison between the glory of Moses and the glory of the Spirit demonstrates parallelism, highlighting contrasting ideas.

questions.question: Which other Bible passage connects to the theme of the vail being removed?
questions.explanation: Hebrews 10:19-20 connects to the theme of the vail being removed, as it discusses the new way opened through Christ.

questions.question: Which other Bible passage echoes the idea of transformation when seeing the Lord's glory?
questions.explanation: 1 John 3:2 echoes the idea of transformation, stating we will be like Him when we see Him as He is, similar to the change mentioned in 2 Corinthians 3:18.

questions.question: What precedes Paul's question about needing letters of commendation?
questions.explanation: Paul's question about needing letters of commendation follows his assertion of confidence through Christ in 2 Corinthians 3:4.

questions.question: What does Paul say about his sufficiency?
questions.explanation: Paul states that our sufficiency is of God, emphasizing reliance on divine support in 2 Corinthians 3:5.

questions.question: The ministration of death was written on what?
questions.explanation: The ministration of death was written and engraven in stones, as noted in 2 Corinthians 3:7.

questions.question: The letter killeth, but what gives life?
questions.explanation: The contrast is made that the letter killeth, but the spirit giveth life, as stated in 2 Corinthians 3:6.

questions.question: True or False: The vail is removed when one turns to the law.
questions.explanation: The vail is taken away when one turns to the Lord, as stated in 2 Corinthians 3:16.

questions.question: True or False: The Spirit of the Lord brings condemnation.
questions.explanation: The Spirit of the Lord brings liberty, not condemnation, as mentioned in 2 Corinthians 3:17.

theological.title: 2 Corinthians Chapter 3 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from 2 Corinthians Chapter 3 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does 2 Corinthians 3:5 teach about human sufficiency in ministry?
options: Our sufficiency is of God, not ourselves
We are sufficient by our own wisdom
Sufficiency comes from rigorous study of the law
Ministers must rely on human strength
questions.correctAnswer: Our sufficiency is of God, not ourselves
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 3:5 states that 'Not that we are sufficient of ourselves to think any thing as of ourselves; but our sufficiency is of God;' showing that human sufficiency in ministry comes from God alone.

questions.question: What doctrine does 2 Corinthians 3:6 teach about the nature of the New Testament ministry?
options: It is a ministry of the spirit, not the letter
It is based on strict adherence to the letter of the law
It relies on external rituals for salvation
It condemns believers for failing the law
questions.correctAnswer: It is a ministry of the spirit, not the letter
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 3:6 highlights that God 'hath made us able ministers of the new testament; not of the letter, but of the spirit: for the letter killeth, but the spirit giveth life.' This teaches that the New Testament ministry is empowered by the Spirit rather than the written law.

questions.question: What doctrine does 2 Corinthians 3:3 teach about the nature of Christian transformation?
options: Believers are the epistle of Christ written in the Spirit on hearts
Transformation is achieved through external adherence to the law
Christian identity depends on physical lineage
Spiritual transformation is only symbolic, not real
questions.correctAnswer: Believers are the epistle of Christ written in the Spirit on hearts
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 3:3 says believers are 'manifestly declared to be the epistle of Christ ministered by us, written not with ink, but with the Spirit of the living God; not in tables of stone, but in fleshy tables of the heart,' teaching that Christian transformation is internal and spiritual.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does 2 Corinthians 3:4 specifically demonstrate?
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 3:4 states 'And such trust have we through Christ to God-ward,' indicating God's faithfulness in enabling and sustaining ministry through Christ.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does 2 Corinthians 3:17 specifically demonstrate?
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 3:17 declares, 'Now the Lord is that Spirit: and where the Spirit of the Lord is, there is liberty,' highlighting God's attribute of granting freedom through the Spirit.

questions.question: How does 2 Corinthians 3:7–8 connect to the broader biblical theme of the transition from Old to New Covenant?
options: It contrasts the fading glory of the Old Covenant with the surpassing glory of the New Covenant
It emphasizes the permanence of the Mosaic Law
It denies any difference between Old and New Covenants
It teaches that the Old Covenant was more glorious than the New
questions.correctAnswer: It contrasts the fading glory of the Old Covenant with the surpassing glory of the New Covenant
questions.explanation: Verses 7 and 8 compare the 'ministration of death' engraved in stone with the 'ministration of the spirit,' showing the greater glory and permanence of the New Covenant ministry, thus preparing for the full revelation of salvation in Christ.

questions.question: How does 2 Corinthians 3:12–13 anticipate the revealing of unveiled truth in the New Testament?
options: By contrasting the veil Moses wore with the openness believers now have
By affirming the continued necessity of the veil
By teaching that the veil remains forever
By denying that Moses ever used a veil
questions.correctAnswer: By contrasting the veil Moses wore with the openness believers now have
questions.explanation: Verses 12-13 describe Moses putting a veil over his face so Israelites could not see the end of what was abolished, setting the stage for the unveiled truth in Christ's ministry.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do verses 14 and 16 teach about spiritual perception and conversion?
options: The veil blinds minds until turning to the Lord, which then removes it
The veil is physical and unrelated to spiritual understanding
Spiritual blindness is permanent even after conversion
The veil is a metaphor for legalism that remains after conversion
questions.correctAnswer: The veil blinds minds until turning to the Lord, which then removes it
questions.explanation: Verse 14 notes minds are blinded by the veil until reading the Old Testament, and verse 16 says when one turns to the Lord, the veil is taken away, teaching that conversion removes spiritual blindness.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do verses 9 and 11 teach about the comparative glory of the covenants?
options: The ministration of righteousness in the New Covenant far exceeds the fading glory of the Old
The New Covenant has no glory compared to the Old
Both covenants have equal and unchanging glory
The Old Covenant remains more glorious than the New
questions.correctAnswer: The ministration of righteousness in the New Covenant far exceeds the fading glory of the Old
questions.explanation: Verse 9 calls the Old Covenant a ministration of condemnation, but the New is of righteousness that exceeds in glory; verse 11 states the New Covenant remains glorious after the Old is done away, showing the surpassing glory of the New.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do verses 2 and 18 teach about the believer's identity and sanctification?
options: Believers are the epistle of Christ and are progressively transformed into His image by the Spirit
Believers are unchanged by the Spirit and remain as before
Believers rely on external letters rather than internal transformation
Sanctification is unrelated to beholding God's glory
questions.correctAnswer: Believers are the epistle of Christ and are progressively transformed into His image by the Spirit
questions.explanation: Verse 2 describes believers as 'our epistle written in our hearts,' and verse 18 teaches they are changed from glory to glory into the Lord's image by the Spirit, highlighting both identity and sanctification.

questions.question: Sceptics claim that 2 Corinthians 3:14–15 teaches the Old Testament is permanently obscured and irrelevant. What does 2 Corinthians 3:14–15 actually teach?
options: The veil remains on hearts reading the Old Testament until one turns to the Lord, implying eventual clarity
The Old Testament is meaningless and should be discarded
The veil is physical and prevents anyone from understanding Scripture
Only the New Testament is inspired and authoritative
questions.correctAnswer: The veil remains on hearts reading the Old Testament until one turns to the Lord, implying eventual clarity
questions.explanation: Verses 14-15 explain the veil remains until turning to Christ, meaning the Old Testament remains spiritually obscured until one embraces Christ, not irrelevant or meaningless.

questions.question: What doctrine does 2 Corinthians 3:1 teach about the nature of apostolic commendation and validation?
options: True commendation comes from the transformed lives of believers, not external letters
Ministers must always provide letters of commendation to be accepted
Validation depends solely on church hierarchy
questions.correctAnswer: True commendation comes from the transformed lives of believers, not external letters
questions.explanation: Verse 1 questions the need for letters of commendation, implying that the Corinthians themselves are the apostolic commendation through their transformation.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does 2 Corinthians 3:16 specifically demonstrate in the context of spiritual enlightenment?
questions.explanation: Verse 16 says 'when it shall turn to the Lord, the vail shall be taken away,' demonstrating God's mercy in removing spiritual blindness for those who turn to Him.

questions.question: How does 2 Corinthians 3:10 prepare for the theological understanding of Christ's superiority over the Old Covenant in Scripture?
options: By emphasizing that the glory of the Old Covenant was surpassed by the glory that excelleth
By teaching that the Old Covenant remains the highest standard of glory
By denying any glory to the Old Covenant
By equating the Old and New Covenants in glory
questions.correctAnswer: By emphasizing that the glory of the Old Covenant was surpassed by the glory that excelleth
questions.explanation: Verse 10 explains that what was glorious in the Old Covenant had no glory when compared to the glory that surpasses it, preparing for the doctrine of Christ's supremacy.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do verses 13 and 17 teach about the contrast between Moses' veiled ministry and the liberating Spirit of the Lord?
options: Moses put a veil over his face limiting perception, but the Lord as Spirit brings liberty where He is present
The veil and Spirit both restrict freedom
The veil remains necessary even in the Spirit's presence
The Spirit replaces the veil with another form of concealment
questions.correctAnswer: Moses put a veil over his face limiting perception, but the Lord as Spirit brings liberty where He is present
questions.explanation: Verse 13 discusses Moses' veiled face, and verse 17 states 'where the Spirit of the Lord is, there is liberty,' showing a movement from concealment to freedom in the new covenant.
